from PIL import Image
import collections

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
w, h = im.size
px = im.load()

# Get average color per column
cols = []
for x in range(w):
    r=g=b=0
    for y in range(h):
        p = px[x,y]
        r+=p[0]; g+=p[1]; b+=p[2]
    n=h
    cols.append((r//n, g//n, b//n))

# Collapse consecutive identical columns into stripes
stripes = []
start = 0
for x in range(1, w+1):
    if x==w or cols[x] != cols[x-1]:
        stripes.append((start, x-start, cols[start]))
        start = x

print("num stripes:", len(stripes))
print("total width:", w)
# Overall brightness stats
import statistics
lum = [0.299*r+0.587*g+0.114*b for (r,g,b) in cols]
print("mean lum:", round(statistics.mean(lum),1), "median:", round(statistics.median(lum),1))
sat = [ (max(c)-min(c)) for c in cols ]
print("mean maxdiff:", round(statistics.mean(sat),1))

# Show stripes with position fraction, width, color
for i,(s,wd,c) in enumerate(stripes):
    frac = s/w
    print(f"{i:3d} pos={frac:.3f} w={wd:4d} rgb={c}")
EOF

"Taki Taki" is a song by French-Algerian DJ and record producer DJ Snake, featuring American singer Selena Gomez, Puerto Rican singer Ozuna, and Dominican-American rapper Cardi B. The song was released on 28 September 2018 as the second single from DJ Snake's second studio album Carte Blanche (2019).[3] It was written and arranged by Bava (aka Ava Brignol), Belcalis Almanzar, Jorden Thorpe, Juan Carlos Ozuna Rosado, Juan G. Rivera, Max Borghetti, Selena Gomez, Vicente Saavedra, William Grigahcine. Ozuna opens the moombahton and reggaetón song in Spanish, while Cardi B and Gomez follow in both English and Spanish.

The song's music video, directed by Colin Tilley, was released on 9 October 2018 and features the four artists and several dancers inside of an ancient temple ruin within a volcano. The single reached number one in sixteen countries (including Argentina, Portugal and Spain), several of which were outside the Hispanophone market. It received a Diamond certification in France, went quadruple Platinum in the US, and won nine music awards. "Taki Taki" made Cardi B the first female rapper to top the Spotify Global chart,[4] extended her record as the first female rapper with multiple billion-streamers on the platform,[5] and made Ozuna the artist with the most one billion-view videos on YouTube.[6]

Background[edit]
In July 2018, Cardi B confirmed a collaboration with DJ Snake, Ozuna and a third mystery guest.[7] The following month, Selena Gomez and Cardi B teased a behind-the-scenes look at the song's music video shoot, which was filmed in Los Angeles.[8][9] On 17 September 2018, DJ Snake announced the release date.[10]

Composition[edit]
"Taki Taki", a reference to percussion and drum beats, is classed primarily as a moombahton and reggaetón song.[11][12][13] The whistle sample (in the hook) is from Sounds of KSHMR Vol.2. The track runs for three minutes and thirty-two seconds. Ozuna opens the track and provides the chorus, while Cardi B and Gomez follow, performing in English and Spanish.[12][14]

Lyrically, the song sees Ozuna expressing his style of seduction, inviting his love interest to dance and interpreting what the other is thinking.[15]

Sheet music for "Taki Taki" showed the key of C♯ minor in common time with a fast tempo of 96 beats per minute.[16]

Music videos[edit]
From left to right, DJ Snake, Selena Gomez, Cardi B and Ozuna performing on an active lava field.
The music video for "Taki Taki" premiered on 9 October 2018 on DJ Snake's YouTube channel. The video was directed by Colin Tilley. A short teaser clip was shown at the 2018 American Music Awards.[17] The video is set in a post-apocalyptic world.[18] The clip transitions with various landscapes showing the quartet together with a volcano in the background and in the solo scenes. These scenes include DJ Snake out in the storm near a Range Rover, Ozuna in a women-filled pit, Cardi B wearing a black bodysuit covered by a black cape accompanied by dancers, and Gomez in a green monochromatic outfit in the forest.[19][20] It became the fifth fastest video of 2018 to reach 100 million views, and ranked among the top 10 fastest overall.[21] "Taki Taki" made Ozuna the artist with the most 1 billion-view videos on YouTube, with over seven videos.[6] As of September 2025, the video has received over 2.7 billion views on YouTube.[22]
 
A pixel video for "Taki Taki" was released on 11 December 2018 on YouTube, which featured animated pixel versions of the four artists dancing in various backgrounds.[23] The lyrics "Booty explota como nagasaki" (Booty blows up like Nagasaki) was criticized by Japanese media for belittling the atomic bombing of Nagasaki and the experience of its survivors.[24][25] The lyrics were changed to "Booty explota como saki saki" (Booty blows up like saki saki), as requested by Universal Music LLC.[26]  This change in the lyrics was made in the official video.
In France, the music video were criticized following suggestive scenes, Cardi B's sexual poses and was broadcast with blurring and a warning "Not advised to kids under 10 years old" or without warning.[citation needed]

Commercial performance[edit]
In the United States, "Taki Taki" debuted at number one on the Hot Latin Songs, where Ozuna replaced himself at the top with "Te Boté", while bowing at number 27 on the Billboard Hot 100.[27] It eventually reached number 11 on the Hot 100 during its fourth week.[28] It became Gomez's 16th consecutive top 40 entry on the Hot 100, the longest active run of any artist.[29] In the US Latin Airplay chart, it became the first number one for both DJ Snake and Gomez, the eighth for Ozuna and third for Cardi B.[30]

In addition, "Taki Taki" reached number one in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Greece, Guatemala, Honduras, Israel, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Portugal, Spain and Venezuela; the song also reached the top 10 in Belgium, Canada, Chile, Costa Rica, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Paraguay, the Philippines, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Sweden and Switzerland; as well as the top 20 in Austria, Finland, Ireland, Lebanon, New Zealand, Norway, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The song had a strong international impact, reaching the top of the Spotify Global 50 chart where it has stayed for over four weeks. This made Cardi B the first female rapper to achieve such a feat.[4] It became DJ Snake's third song to reach a billion streams on Spotify, as well as Cardi's third and Gomez's and Ozuna's first.[31] Cardi B extended her record as the first female rapper with multiple billion-streamers, until being surpassed by black females rappers Nicki Minaj (7 songs) and Doja Cat (8 songs).[5] As of November 2018, the song has reached number one on the official charts of 15 countries and the top 10 of 33 countries around the world.

In France, the song debuted at number thirteen on September 26, 2018, becoming for three of four artists the highest-debut since Gomez's own solo song "Good For You", served as the lead single from her second album Revival, which debuted at number 14.
Several weeks later and after Christmas time, the song peaked at number 2 on January 5, 2019, blocked by "Tout Oublier" by Belgian artist Angèle becoming DJ Snake's sixth top ten, Gomez's third, Cardi B's second and last top ten and Ozuna's first top ten.[32]

Although it failed to peak atop, the single is currently certified diamond in France and spent 57 weeks, becoming Ozuna, Gomez's and Cardi B longest-running song and DJ Snake second longest running song after "Loco Contigo".

Live performances[edit]
Ozuna and Cardi B performed the song together live for the first time at the Dominican Republic's Electric Paradise Festival on 22 December 2018.[33] Ozuna also performed the song at the 2019 Premios Lo Nuestro.[34] On 15 March 2019, he performed the song as part of a medley with "Baila Baila Baila" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. The only time in which all four artists—DJ Snake, Ozuna, Cardi B and Selena Gomez—took to the stage together was during DJ Snake's set at the 2019 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival in Indio, California, much to the audience’s excitement. Ozuna featured the song during his headlining set and livestreamed performance at the Viña Del Mar International Song Festival, in Valparaíso, Chile, on 28 February 2020.[35] He also performed the song during the Celebrating America inauguration special in 2021.[36]

"Taki Taki" is a song by French-Algerian DJ and record producer DJ Snake, featuring American singer Selena Gomez, Puerto Rican singer Ozuna, and Dominican-American rapper Cardi B. The song was released on 28 September 2018 as the second single from DJ Snake's second studio album Carte Blanche (2019).[3] It was written and arranged by Bava (aka Ava Brignol), Belcalis Almanzar, Jorden Thorpe, Juan Carlos Ozuna Rosado, Juan G. Rivera, Max Borghetti, Selena Gomez, Vicente Saavedra, William Grigahcine. Ozuna opens the moombahton and reggaetón song in Spanish, while Cardi B and Gomez follow in both English and Spanish.

The song's music video, directed by Colin Tilley, was released on 9 October 2018 and features the four artists and several dancers inside of an ancient temple ruin within a volcano. The single reached number one in sixteen countries (including Argentina, Portugal and Spain), several of which were outside the Hispanophone market. It received a Diamond certification in France, went quadruple Platinum in the US, and won nine music awards. "Taki Taki" made Cardi B the first female rapper to top the Spotify Global chart,[4] extended her record as the first female rapper with multiple billion-streamers on the platform,[5] and made Ozuna the artist with the most one billion-view videos on YouTube.[6]

Background[edit]
In July 2018, Cardi B confirmed a collaboration with DJ Snake, Ozuna and a third mystery guest.[7] The following month, Selena Gomez and Cardi B teased a behind-the-scenes look at the song's music video shoot, which was filmed in Los Angeles.[8][9] On 17 September 2018, DJ Snake announced the release date.[10]

Composition[edit]
"Taki Taki", a reference to percussion and drum beats, is classed primarily as a moombahton and reggaetón song.[11][12][13] The whistle sample (in the hook) is from Sounds of KSHMR Vol.2. The track runs for three minutes and thirty-two seconds. Ozuna opens the track and provides the chorus, while Cardi B and Gomez follow, performing in English and Spanish.[12][14]

Lyrically, the song sees Ozuna expressing his style of seduction, inviting his love interest to dance and interpreting what the other is thinking.[15]

Sheet music for "Taki Taki" showed the key of C♯ minor in common time with a fast tempo of 96 beats per minute.[16]

Music videos[edit]
From left to right, DJ Snake, Selena Gomez, Cardi B and Ozuna performing on an active lava field.
The music video for "Taki Taki" premiered on 9 October 2018 on DJ Snake's YouTube channel. The video was directed by Colin Tilley. A short teaser clip was shown at the 2018 American Music Awards.[17] The video is set in a post-apocalyptic world.[18] The clip transitions with various landscapes showing the quartet together with a volcano in the background and in the solo scenes. These scenes include DJ Snake out in the storm near a Range Rover, Ozuna in a women-filled pit, Cardi B wearing a black bodysuit covered by a black cape accompanied by dancers, and Gomez in a green monochromatic outfit in the forest.[19][20] It became the fifth fastest video of 2018 to reach 100 million views, and ranked among the top 10 fastest overall.[21] "Taki Taki" made Ozuna the artist with the most 1 billion-view videos on YouTube, with over seven videos.[6] As of September 2025, the video has received over 2.7 billion views on YouTube.[22]
 
A pixel video for "Taki Taki" was released on 11 December 2018 on YouTube, which featured animated pixel versions of the four artists dancing in various backgrounds.[23] The lyrics "Booty explota como nagasaki" (Booty blows up like Nagasaki) was criticized by Japanese media for belittling the atomic bombing of Nagasaki and the experience of its survivors.[24][25] The lyrics were changed to "Booty explota como saki saki" (Booty blows up like saki saki), as requested by Universal Music LLC.[26]  This change in the lyrics was made in the official video.
In France, the music video were criticized following suggestive scenes, Cardi B's sexual poses and was broadcast with blurring and a warning "Not advised to kids under 10 years old" or without warning.[citation needed]

Commercial performance[edit]
In the United States, "Taki Taki" debuted at number one on the Hot Latin Songs, where Ozuna replaced himself at the top with "Te Boté", while bowing at number 27 on the Billboard Hot 100.[27] It eventually reached number 11 on the Hot 100 during its fourth week.[28] It became Gomez's 16th consecutive top 40 entry on the Hot 100, the longest active run of any artist.[29] In the US Latin Airplay chart, it became the first number one for both DJ Snake and Gomez, the eighth for Ozuna and third for Cardi B.[30]

In addition, "Taki Taki" reached number one in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Greece, Guatemala, Honduras, Israel, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Portugal, Spain and Venezuela; the song also reached the top 10 in Belgium, Canada, Chile, Costa Rica, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Paraguay, the Philippines, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Sweden and Switzerland; as well as the top 20 in Austria, Finland, Ireland, Lebanon, New Zealand, Norway, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The song had a strong international impact, reaching the top of the Spotify Global 50 chart where it has stayed for over four weeks. This made Cardi B the first female rapper to achieve such a feat.[4] It became DJ Snake's third song to reach a billion streams on Spotify, as well as Cardi's third and Gomez's and Ozuna's first.[31] Cardi B extended her record as the first female rapper with multiple billion-streamers, until being surpassed by black females rappers Nicki Minaj (7 songs) and Doja Cat (8 songs).[5] As of November 2018, the song has reached number one on the official charts of 15 countries and the top 10 of 33 countries around the world.

In France, the song debuted at number thirteen on September 26, 2018, becoming for three of four artists the highest-debut since Gomez's own solo song "Good For You", served as the lead single from her second album Revival, which debuted at number 14.
Several weeks later and after Christmas time, the song peaked at number 2 on January 5, 2019, blocked by "Tout Oublier" by Belgian artist Angèle becoming DJ Snake's sixth top ten, Gomez's third, Cardi B's second and last top ten and Ozuna's first top ten.[32]

Although it failed to peak atop, the single is currently certified diamond in France and spent 57 weeks, becoming Ozuna, Gomez's and Cardi B longest-running song and DJ Snake second longest running song after "Loco Contigo".

Live performances[edit]
Ozuna and Cardi B performed the song together live for the first time at the Dominican Republic's Electric Paradise Festival on 22 December 2018.[33] Ozuna also performed the song at the 2019 Premios Lo Nuestro.[34] On 15 March 2019, he performed the song as part of a medley with "Baila Baila Baila" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. The only time in which all four artists—DJ Snake, Ozuna, Cardi B and Selena Gomez—took to the stage together was during DJ Snake's set at the 2019 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival in Indio, California, much to the audience’s excitement. Ozuna featured the song during his headlining set and livestreamed performance at the Viña Del Mar International Song Festival, in Valparaíso, Chile, on 28 February 2020.[35] He also performed the song during the Celebrating America inauguration special in 2021.[36]

"Felices los 4" (transl. "Happy the 4 of Us")[1] is a song by Colombian singer Maluma from his third studio album, F.A.M.E. (2018). It was released by Sony Music Latin on 21 April 2017. The track was written by Maluma, Servando Primera, Mario Cáceres and Miky La Sensa, and produced by Rude Boyz.[2] A salsa version of the song featuring American singer Marc Anthony and produced by Sergio George was released on 7 July 2017.[3] "Felices los 4" became Maluma's first single as lead artist to appear on the US Billboard Hot 100, where it charted for 20 weeks and peaked at number 48.

Music video[edit]
Directed by Jessy Terrero, the accompanying music video follows a love triangle between Maluma, a married woman played by actress and model Natalia Barulich and her husband, portrayed by Wilmer Valderrama.[4] On 5 May 2017, the singer received a Vevo certification because the video became the most watched Latin video worldwide within its first 24 hours.[5]

As of September 2025, the video has been viewed more than 1.9 billion times on YouTube.[6][7]

Salsa version[edit]
A music video for the salsa version of the song featuring American singer Marc Anthony was released on 11 August 2017 and filmed in Miami's El Tucán and Marion. It was also directed by Terrero and the video continues the plot from the music video of the original version featuring Wilmer Valderrama, Natalia Barulich and model and actress Priscilla Huggins.[8]

"Felices los 4" (transl. "Happy the 4 of Us")[1] is a song by Colombian singer Maluma from his third studio album, F.A.M.E. (2018). It was released by Sony Music Latin on 21 April 2017. The track was written by Maluma, Servando Primera, Mario Cáceres and Miky La Sensa, and produced by Rude Boyz.[2] A salsa version of the song featuring American singer Marc Anthony and produced by Sergio George was released on 7 July 2017.[3] "Felices los 4" became Maluma's first single as lead artist to appear on the US Billboard Hot 100, where it charted for 20 weeks and peaked at number 48.

Music video[edit]
Directed by Jessy Terrero, the accompanying music video follows a love triangle between Maluma, a married woman played by actress and model Natalia Barulich and her husband, portrayed by Wilmer Valderrama.[4] On 5 May 2017, the singer received a Vevo certification because the video became the most watched Latin video worldwide within its first 24 hours.[5]

As of September 2025, the video has been viewed more than 1.9 billion times on YouTube.[6][7]

Salsa version[edit]
A music video for the salsa version of the song featuring American singer Marc Anthony was released on 11 August 2017 and filmed in Miami's El Tucán and Marion. It was also directed by Terrero and the video continues the plot from the music video of the original version featuring Wilmer Valderrama, Natalia Barulich and model and actress Priscilla Huggins.[8]

"Criminal" is a song by Dominican singer Natti Natasha and Puerto Rican singer Ozuna, released by Pina Records on 18 August 2017. Written by the two singers, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze, it is a reggaeton song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the dancehall genre. The accompanying music video was directed by Nuno Gómes at an abandoned women's prison in Vega Alta, Puerto Rico, and portrays Ozuna as a prison director falling in love with a prisoner played by Natasha. It received over 1 billion views on YouTube within five months of its release and was the most watched music video by a female singer in 2017.

The track was well received by music critics who found it catchy and praised it for giving reggaeton dance floor appeal. It received a number of award nominations, winning Best Collaboration at the 2018 Soberano Awards. "Criminal" became a crossover success and helped relaunch Natasha's music career, becoming her first top five single on the US Hot Latin Songs chart since 2012's "Dutty Love" and first chart-topper in Spain where it spent three consecutive weeks at number one. It also topped the charts in El Salvador, Paraguay, Peru and Spain, and reached the top 10 in 10 other Latin American countries.

Background[edit]
"Criminal" was written by Natasha, Ozuna, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze.[1][2] Pina, Natasha's manager, sent Ozuna the song after two previously failed collaboration attempts, and Ozuna called it a "home run".[3] Pina recalled, "After several months of trying to bring up the song, there was always a situation that would have discouraged anybody but, unlike me, I never got up with a 'no' in my head and continued without anything or anyone stopping me."[3] Natasha regards "Criminal" as her second chance at a career in music and her first solo release where she had sufficient record label support. Regarding the writing process, she said: "To me, it's such a special song because I had the opportunity to write my part of the lyrics and I just really loved it. When Ozuna agreed, I was extremely excited and for some reason, I knew people were going to love it as much as we did."[4]

It is a reggaeton song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the dancehall genre.[3][5]

Music video[edit]
Ozuna approaching Natasha in an electric chair for a kiss in the music video.
The accompanying music video was directed by Venezuelan director Nuno Gómes. It was filmed at a deactivated women's prison in Vega Alta, Puerto Rico in April 2017 and inspired by the music video for Lady Gaga's "Telephone".[6][7] A storm hit Vega Alta a day before the video shoot, resulting in trucks getting stuck in mud and the video wardrobe getting wet. Gómes called it the worst filming day of his career.[6] Filming took nearly 20 hours.[3] Fashion designer Nelson Tavárez chose bold ensembles for Natasha's wardrobe to portray her character as empowered and confident.[8]

Natasha plays a prisoner trying to attract the attention of Ozuna, the prison director.[7] The clip starts with Natasha being escorted to the prison where Ozuna awaits. They are shown in several locations inside the prison with Natasha performing sensual dances for Ozuna. The video reaches a climax with Natasha sitting in an electric chair and Ozuna approaching her for a kiss. Both are struck by electricity, but are shown together amid police alarms in the final scene.[9]

The video led YouTube's weekly chart for two consecutive weeks in November 2017, ending Luis Fonsi's 35-week run at number one with "Despacito".[10][11][12] It surpassed 1 billion views on YouTube within five months of its 18 August 2017 release and was the most watched music video by a female artist in 2017.[6][13] "Criminal" is one of the 100 most viewed videos and eight most viewed Spanish-language videos on YouTube,[14][15] having received over 2.7 billion views as of November 2025.[16] It is also both Natasha and Ozuna's most watched music video on the platform.[16][17] Natasha said YouTube provided her with "the opportunity to reach other parts of the world, when before we depended on a label for that. It's definitely an achievement not only for me, but for Latina women. Before we did not have that reach."[10] Billboard included "Criminal" at number 11 in its list of Top 25 Sexiest Latin Music Videos.[18] Tommy Calle of Hoy wrote that Natasha's "sensuality and beauty" in the video "stands out to the eye".[19]

Critical reception[edit]
"Criminal" was well received by music critics. Leila Cobo of Billboard described the song as "sexy without being vulgar" and said its "immediate catchiness" made it "a YouTube sensation".[20] Marjua Esteves of the same website wrote that it is "not your everyday fast-pumping reggaeton record, but a criminally slow-grinding jam".[21]  Raquel Reichard of The Fader called the track a "knockout" and an "earworm".[22] Writing for Maxim, Brandon Friederich found the song "contagious" and wrote, "Even if you're a non-Spanish speaker, just try resisting the urge to sing the 'muy criminal'-laden chorus".[23] Los 40's Alberto Palao Murcia commented, "I timidly gave the track a play expecting a more Latin rhythm that does not even reach the dance floor, but, to my surprise, by the second chorus I was already singing 'Criminal, Cri-Criminal..."[3] Similarly, Tommy Calle of Hoy called it "an urban anthem that has managed to turn on the dance floor",[24] and "a catchy song that lifts everyone's spirits".[19]

Billboard placed "Criminal" at number 17 in its list of Top 20 Best Latin Songs of 2017.[21] Idolator's Mike Wass gave the song an honorable mention in his list of The Best Latin Pop Songs of 2017.[25]

Live performances[edit]
Natasha and Ozuna performed "Criminal" together at Calibash LA 2018 on 20 January and at the Soberano Awards on 21 March 2018.[26][30] On 21 June 2018, Natasha performed the song at VidCon in Anaheim, California.[31] She also performed the track at KLVE's Las Qué Mandan event at the Inglewood Forum on 17 November 2018.[32]

					2017 single by Natti Natasha and Ozuna

"Criminal"Single by Natti Natasha and OzunaLanguageSpanishReleased18 August 2017 (2017-08-18)GenreReggaetonLength3:52LabelPinaSongwritersNatalia GutiérrezJuan Carlos OzunaEgbert RosaJesús NievesRafael PinaVicente SaavedraProducerHazeNatti Natasha singles chronology

Music video"Criminal" on YouTube


"Criminal" is a song by Dominican singer Natti Natasha and Puerto Rican singer Ozuna, released by Pina Records on 18 August 2017. Written by the two singers, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze, it is a reggaeton song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the dancehall genre. The accompanying music video was directed by Nuno Gómes at an abandoned women's prison in Vega Alta, Puerto Rico, and portrays Ozuna as a prison director falling in love with a prisoner played by Natasha. It received over 1 billion views on YouTube within five months of its release and was the most watched music video by a female singer in 2017.

The track was well received by music critics who found it catchy and praised it for giving reggaeton dance floor appeal. It received a number of award nominations, winning Best Collaboration at the 2018 Soberano Awards. "Criminal" became a crossover success and helped relaunch Natasha's music career, becoming her first top five single on the US Hot Latin Songs chart since 2012's "Dutty Love" and first chart-topper in Spain where it spent three consecutive weeks at number one. It also topped the charts in El Salvador, Paraguay, Peru and Spain, and reached the top 10 in 10 other Latin American countries.

Background[edit]
"Criminal" was written by Natasha, Ozuna, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze.[1][2] Pina, Natasha's manager, sent Ozuna the song after two previously failed collaboration attempts, and Ozuna called it a "home run".[3] Pina recalled, "After several months of trying to bring up the song, there was always a situation that would have discouraged anybody but, unlike me, I never got up with a 'no' in my head and continued without anything or anyone stopping me."[3] Natasha regards "Criminal" as her second chance at a career in music and her first solo release where she had sufficient record label support. Regarding the writing process, she said: "To me, it's such a special song because I had the opportunity to write my part of the lyrics and I just really loved it. When Ozuna agreed, I was extremely excited and for some reason, I knew people were going to love it as much as we did."[4]

It is a reggaeton song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the dancehall genre.[3][5]

Music video[edit]
Ozuna approaching Natasha in an electric chair for a kiss in the music video.
The accompanying music video was directed by Venezuelan director Nuno Gómes. It was filmed at a deactivated women's prison in Vega Alta, Puerto Rico in April 2017 and inspired by the music video for Lady Gaga's "Telephone".[6][7] A storm hit Vega Alta a day before the video shoot, resulting in trucks getting stuck in mud and the video wardrobe getting wet. Gómes called it the worst filming day of his career.[6] Filming took nearly 20 hours.[3] Fashion designer Nelson Tavárez chose bold ensembles for Natasha's wardrobe to portray her character as empowered and confident.[8]

Natasha plays a prisoner trying to attract the attention of Ozuna, the prison director.[7] The clip starts with Natasha being escorted to the prison where Ozuna awaits. They are shown in several locations inside the prison with Natasha performing sensual dances for Ozuna. The video reaches a climax with Natasha sitting in an electric chair and Ozuna approaching her for a kiss. Both are struck by electricity, but are shown together amid police alarms in the final scene.[9]

The video led YouTube's weekly chart for two consecutive weeks in November 2017, ending Luis Fonsi's 35-week run at number one with "Despacito".[10][11][12] It surpassed 1 billion views on YouTube within five months of its 18 August 2017 release and was the most watched music video by a female artist in 2017.[6][13] "Criminal" is one of the 100 most viewed videos and eight most viewed Spanish-language videos on YouTube,[14][15] having received over 2.7 billion views as of November 2025.[16] It is also both Natasha and Ozuna's most watched music video on the platform.[16][17] Natasha said YouTube provided her with "the opportunity to reach other parts of the world, when before we depended on a label for that. It's definitely an achievement not only for me, but for Latina women. Before we did not have that reach."[10] Billboard included "Criminal" at number 11 in its list of Top 25 Sexiest Latin Music Videos.[18] Tommy Calle of Hoy wrote that Natasha's "sensuality and beauty" in the video "stands out to the eye".[19]

Critical reception[edit]
"Criminal" was well received by music critics. Leila Cobo of Billboard described the song as "sexy without being vulgar" and said its "immediate catchiness" made it "a YouTube sensation".[20] Marjua Esteves of the same website wrote that it is "not your everyday fast-pumping reggaeton record, but a criminally slow-grinding jam".[21]  Raquel Reichard of The Fader called the track a "knockout" and an "earworm".[22] Writing for Maxim, Brandon Friederich found the song "contagious" and wrote, "Even if you're a non-Spanish speaker, just try resisting the urge to sing the 'muy criminal'-laden chorus".[23] Los 40's Alberto Palao Murcia commented, "I timidly gave the track a play expecting a more Latin rhythm that does not even reach the dance floor, but, to my surprise, by the second chorus I was already singing 'Criminal, Cri-Criminal..."[3] Similarly, Tommy Calle of Hoy called it "an urban anthem that has managed to turn on the dance floor",[24] and "a catchy song that lifts everyone's spirits".[19]

Billboard placed "Criminal" at number 17 in its list of Top 20 Best Latin Songs of 2017.[21] Idolator's Mike Wass gave the song an honorable mention in his list of The Best Latin Pop Songs of 2017.[25]

Live performances[edit]
Natasha and Ozuna performed "Criminal" together at Calibash LA 2018 on 20 January and at the Soberano Awards on 21 March 2018.[26][30] On 21 June 2018, Natasha performed the song at VidCon in Anaheim, California.[31] She also performed the track at KLVE's Las Qué Mandan event at the Inglewood Forum on 17 November 2018.[32]

"Chantaje" (Spanish pronunciation: [tʃanˈtaxe]; English: "Blackmail") is a song by the Colombian singer-songwriter Shakira featuring Maluma. It was released on October 28, 2016, via Sony Music Latin, as the lead single from Shakira's eleventh album, El Dorado (2017). The song was written by Shakira and Maluma and produced by them and the Rudeboyz, with musical composition assistance from Kenai. The song is Maluma and Shakira's second collaboration after a remix of Carlos Vives' single "La Bicicleta".

"Chantaje" is a pop and reggaeton song. Lyrically, the song was considered a "battle of the sexes", where the male protagonist is not sure where he stands with his lover, and the female protagonist does not exactly clear things up. The music video for "Chantaje" was filmed in Barcelona, Spain, with video director Jaume de Laiguana, Shakira's long-time collaborator.

Commercially, the song topped the Brazil, Ecuador, Guatemala, Spain, Uruguay, and US Billboard Latin Songs charts, while also reaching the top five in nine additional countries. Maluma called it his "first global hit".[1] It became the most successful Latin single of the decade by a female artist in the United States.[2] The track is also certified Platinum or higher in ten countries, including Diamond in Argentina, Brazil (three times), Colombia, France, Mexico and United States (Latin). The song was nominated for Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best Urban Fusion Performance at the 18th Latin Grammy Awards.[3]

Background and release[edit]
Puerto Rican composer and recording artist Kenai had the word "Chantaje" in his mind months before the idea of a collaboration with Shakira and Maluma emerged.[4] He stated in an interview that the idea of the song was intended to be his own single.[5] While working on music demos in Colombia with The Rudeboyz, he received a call from the production duo to work on a collaborative single between Shakira and Maluma that was intended to be presented to the artists the next day. They were supposed to offer three different demos to Shakira and Maluma, but ended up working on just one feeling confident enough about its potential. The three worked together on the demo one night in Colombia. The Rudeboyz traveled without Kenai the next day to Barcelona, Spain to meet with Shakira and Maluma to keep working on the song together.[4]

Before collaborating with Shakira in "Chantaje", Maluma served guest vocals for the official remix of Carlos Vives and Shakira's 2016 song "La Bicicleta".[6] Later, Maluma travelled to Barcelona in early September 2016 to work with Shakira, along with his production team. He confessed to Billboard that "he couldn't miss the opportunity to work with [her] again." The pairing was possible due to Sony Music Latin, who proposed the idea for both artists working together again after the remix of "La Bicicleta".[7] Maluma also commented about Shakira, stating: "It was an amazing experience. [...] She's a great artist, but she's also a composer. I learned a lot."[8]

Before releasing the song, Shakira shared clues on her Instagram account on 25 October 2016, and if someone solved the mystery, they would get a personal message from the singer confirming the correct answer.[9] The first photo had Shakira "wearing a magician's hat and holding a rabbit," which meant "Magic", name of both Shakira's and Maluma's first albums; the second photo had a drawing of a crown in a white board, meaning Maluma's crown tattoo; and the third photo was Shakira holding a poster with a photo of Alejandro Sanz (which stands for his nickname "Chan") + TA + G, which was the title of the track: "Chantaje", literally "blackmail."[9][10] Later, the singer shared the artwork of the single, featuring both artists.[9] Eventually, the song was released on 28 October 2016 through digital download by Ace Entertainment.[11]

Composition[edit]
"Chantaje" was written by Shakira, Maluma, Kenai and production duo The Rudeboyz. It was also produced by Shakira and Maluma with The Rudeboyz.[12] "Chantaje" is a pop and reggaeton song,[13][7] with tropical synths in its background.[14] The song is built from a "pitched-up vocal" saying "Hola, mira" ("Hello, look").[15] Lyrically, the song is a chase "between a lustful man and an unattainable woman,"[16] where "he’s not sure where he stands with her, and she's not exactly clearing things up."[15] "Yo soy masoquista" ("I'm a masochist"), he says, and she responds, "Con mi cuerpo, un egoísta" ("With my body, [you're] a selfish [man]"); later, she reassures him: "Te dicen [...] que en esta relación, soy yo la que manda [...] esa mala propaganda" ("They say that... in this relationship, I’m in command... that's just evil propaganda").[15] In the chorus, to the contrary, she asserts: "No soy de ti ni de nadie" ("I'm not yours or anyone else's").[16]

Critical reception[edit]
Jon Pareles of The New York Times was positive, noting that "Shakira gets even more intense when she sings in Spanish, nervier and more committed," and calling the song "a sparse, insinuatingly catchy reggaetón battle of the sexes."[15] Jeff Nelson of People named it "a sexy, buoyant jam,"[17] while Diana Martin of E! Online wrote that the song is "all sorts of sexy and infectious."[18] Lucy Morris of Digital Spy admitted: "We may have no clue what the lyrics mean, but the song is infectious."[13] Mike Wass of Idolator opined that the song "is instantly hummable regardless of your Spanish language skills and will have you moving before the end of the first verse. It’s a winner and has the potential to be a 'La Tortura'-sized crossover hit."[19] Lucas Villa of AXS said that the song "plays to Shakira's strengths as a global seductress with a banger that's ready to make club-goers bend to its will."[14]

Billboard included Chantaje among the 50 essential Latin songs of the 2010s decade.[20]

Commercial performance[edit]

In the United States, the song became the second track to ever debut atop Billboard Top Latin Songs after Shakira's and Maná's "Mi Verdad", after the chart became a multi-metric chart. With its first-week sales of 13,000 digital downloads, 1.6 million streams and 13.8 million audience impressions in the US, the song became the second highest sales week for a Spanish-language track in 2016.[21] The single was "only the 14th track to debut atop the chart in its 30-year history"Chantaje", as reported by Billboard.[22] It is also Shakira's eleventh number-one on the chart, and Maluma's first. "Chantaje" also debuted at number 96 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, becoming Shakira's 19th entry there and Maluma's first.[22] In its eighth charting week, the song managed to jump from number 65 to number 51, becoming her highest Hot 100 Spanish-language single after "La Tortura" (2005).[23] In the same week, the song spent its eighth non-consecutive week at the top of the Latin Songs, matching the amount of time that "Hips Don't Lie" spent in 2006, while also becoming her second longest chart reign, spending eleven weeks at number one.[23] It has been certified 16× Platinum by the RIAA's Latin certifications program, denoting sales of over 960,000 units.[24] According to the 2017 year-end Nielsen Canada report, the song has sold 177,000 units in the country.[25] "Chantaje" went on to become the most successful Latin single of the decade by a female artist in the United States, according to Billboard.[2]

In the United Kingdom, the single became the first Spanish song by a female artist in history to be certified Silver for surpassing 200,000 equivalent units in the country.[26]
 
In France, the song debuted at number 36 on the week of 11 November 2016.[27] Later, it fell to numbers 91 and 126 in the following weeks, before climbing once again to number 76. After spending three weeks climbing on the charts, "Chantaje" cracked the top-forty for the second time, going to number forty.[27] Five weeks later, the song managed to climb from number 22 to number 14,[28] becoming Shakira's fifteenth top-twenty single and highest since "Dare (La La La)" (2014).

In Italy, "Chantaje" debuted at number 15 and peaked at number 11 for two weeks.[29]

In Netherlands, "Chantaje" managed to peak at number 18, becoming her highest-charting single since "Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)" (2010).[30]
 
In Switzerland, the song peaked at number 10, becoming Shakira's fifteenth top-ten single.[31]
 
In Spain, "Chantaje" entered the PROMUSICAE chart at number eight and reached number-one the following week, becoming Shakira's eighth number-one single.[32]

Music video[edit]
The music video was shot in Barcelona, on 13 and 14 October 2016, and it was directed by Spanish director and photographer Jaume de Laiguana, who has already directed various Shakira's music videos.[18] Cinematography was handled by Spanish cinematographer Xavi Giménez.[33] The official lyric video to the song was released on 16 November,[34] while the official music video was released on 18 November 2016.[35] In the beginning of the music video, as described by Rolling Stone's Sarah Grant, "Shakira strolls through a bodega with her pet pig on a leash and her wild mane of hair hidden under a pink wig."[16] "She then lures him in to an underground bar", as Billboard added,[35] while also "swivel[ing] her hips from the top of the bar to the men's bathroom, where she winds, kicks and grinds solo amid the urinals."[16]

Reception[edit]
The music video earned 100 million views in just 19 days, breaking the previous 21 days record, and becoming the fastest Spanish video ever to do so.[36] On 7 April 2017, it reached 1 billion views, becoming the fastest Spanish video to hit the billion visits landmark.[37] It was also the second-most viewed video on Vevo in 2017, after "Despacito".[38]

Salsa version[edit]
On 2 February, Shakira celebrated her birthday with a salsa version of "Chantaje" with Chelito de Castro.[39][40]

Live performances[edit]
Maluma performed the song in Valparaíso at the Viña del Mar International Song Festival in February 2017, then on his various tours since, where he typically has a female vocalist stand-in for Shakira's vocals. 

Shakira performed "Chantaje" with Coldplay's lead vocalist Chris Martin at the Global Citizen Festival in Hamburg in July 2017. She tried to get him to sing and understand the Spanish words. Shakira subsequently performed the song, solo, during her El Dorado World Tour in 2018.

Shakira performed a shortened, Salsa-inspired version of the song with Bad Bunny during her medley of songs at the Super Bowl LIV halftime show in 2020.[41][42]

On 12 April 2025, Shakira and Maluma performed the song together for the very first time during Shakira’s Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour in Medellin.[43]

"Chantaje" (Spanish pronunciation: [tʃanˈtaxe]; English: "Blackmail") is a song by the Colombian singer-songwriter Shakira featuring Maluma. It was released on October 28, 2016, via Sony Music Latin, as the lead single from Shakira's eleventh album, El Dorado (2017). The song was written by Shakira and Maluma and produced by them and the Rudeboyz, with musical composition assistance from Kenai. The song is Maluma and Shakira's second collaboration after a remix of Carlos Vives' single "La Bicicleta".

"Chantaje" is a pop and reggaeton song. Lyrically, the song was considered a "battle of the sexes", where the male protagonist is not sure where he stands with his lover, and the female protagonist does not exactly clear things up. The music video for "Chantaje" was filmed in Barcelona, Spain, with video director Jaume de Laiguana, Shakira's long-time collaborator.

Commercially, the song topped the Brazil, Ecuador, Guatemala, Spain, Uruguay, and US Billboard Latin Songs charts, while also reaching the top five in nine additional countries. Maluma called it his "first global hit".[1] It became the most successful Latin single of the decade by a female artist in the United States.[2] The track is also certified Platinum or higher in ten countries, including Diamond in Argentina, Brazil (three times), Colombia, France, Mexico and United States (Latin). The song was nominated for Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best Urban Fusion Performance at the 18th Latin Grammy Awards.[3]

Background and release[edit]
Puerto Rican composer and recording artist Kenai had the word "Chantaje" in his mind months before the idea of a collaboration with Shakira and Maluma emerged.[4] He stated in an interview that the idea of the song was intended to be his own single.[5] While working on music demos in Colombia with The Rudeboyz, he received a call from the production duo to work on a collaborative single between Shakira and Maluma that was intended to be presented to the artists the next day. They were supposed to offer three different demos to Shakira and Maluma, but ended up working on just one feeling confident enough about its potential. The three worked together on the demo one night in Colombia. The Rudeboyz traveled without Kenai the next day to Barcelona, Spain to meet with Shakira and Maluma to keep working on the song together.[4]

Before collaborating with Shakira in "Chantaje", Maluma served guest vocals for the official remix of Carlos Vives and Shakira's 2016 song "La Bicicleta".[6] Later, Maluma travelled to Barcelona in early September 2016 to work with Shakira, along with his production team. He confessed to Billboard that "he couldn't miss the opportunity to work with [her] again." The pairing was possible due to Sony Music Latin, who proposed the idea for both artists working together again after the remix of "La Bicicleta".[7] Maluma also commented about Shakira, stating: "It was an amazing experience. [...] She's a great artist, but she's also a composer. I learned a lot."[8]

Before releasing the song, Shakira shared clues on her Instagram account on 25 October 2016, and if someone solved the mystery, they would get a personal message from the singer confirming the correct answer.[9] The first photo had Shakira "wearing a magician's hat and holding a rabbit," which meant "Magic", name of both Shakira's and Maluma's first albums; the second photo had a drawing of a crown in a white board, meaning Maluma's crown tattoo; and the third photo was Shakira holding a poster with a photo of Alejandro Sanz (which stands for his nickname "Chan") + TA + G, which was the title of the track: "Chantaje", literally "blackmail."[9][10] Later, the singer shared the artwork of the single, featuring both artists.[9] Eventually, the song was released on 28 October 2016 through digital download by Ace Entertainment.[11]

Composition[edit]
"Chantaje" was written by Shakira, Maluma, Kenai and production duo The Rudeboyz. It was also produced by Shakira and Maluma with The Rudeboyz.[12] "Chantaje" is a pop and reggaeton song,[13][7] with tropical synths in its background.[14] The song is built from a "pitched-up vocal" saying "Hola, mira" ("Hello, look").[15] Lyrically, the song is a chase "between a lustful man and an unattainable woman,"[16] where "he’s not sure where he stands with her, and she's not exactly clearing things up."[15] "Yo soy masoquista" ("I'm a masochist"), he says, and she responds, "Con mi cuerpo, un egoísta" ("With my body, [you're] a selfish [man]"); later, she reassures him: "Te dicen [...] que en esta relación, soy yo la que manda [...] esa mala propaganda" ("They say that... in this relationship, I’m in command... that's just evil propaganda").[15] In the chorus, to the contrary, she asserts: "No soy de ti ni de nadie" ("I'm not yours or anyone else's").[16]

Critical reception[edit]
Jon Pareles of The New York Times was positive, noting that "Shakira gets even more intense when she sings in Spanish, nervier and more committed," and calling the song "a sparse, insinuatingly catchy reggaetón battle of the sexes."[15] Jeff Nelson of People named it "a sexy, buoyant jam,"[17] while Diana Martin of E! Online wrote that the song is "all sorts of sexy and infectious."[18] Lucy Morris of Digital Spy admitted: "We may have no clue what the lyrics mean, but the song is infectious."[13] Mike Wass of Idolator opined that the song "is instantly hummable regardless of your Spanish language skills and will have you moving before the end of the first verse. It’s a winner and has the potential to be a 'La Tortura'-sized crossover hit."[19] Lucas Villa of AXS said that the song "plays to Shakira's strengths as a global seductress with a banger that's ready to make club-goers bend to its will."[14]

Billboard included Chantaje among the 50 essential Latin songs of the 2010s decade.[20]

Commercial performance[edit]

In the United States, the song became the second track to ever debut atop Billboard Top Latin Songs after Shakira's and Maná's "Mi Verdad", after the chart became a multi-metric chart. With its first-week sales of 13,000 digital downloads, 1.6 million streams and 13.8 million audience impressions in the US, the song became the second highest sales week for a Spanish-language track in 2016.[21] The single was "only the 14th track to debut atop the chart in its 30-year history"Chantaje", as reported by Billboard.[22] It is also Shakira's eleventh number-one on the chart, and Maluma's first. "Chantaje" also debuted at number 96 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, becoming Shakira's 19th entry there and Maluma's first.[22] In its eighth charting week, the song managed to jump from number 65 to number 51, becoming her highest Hot 100 Spanish-language single after "La Tortura" (2005).[23] In the same week, the song spent its eighth non-consecutive week at the top of the Latin Songs, matching the amount of time that "Hips Don't Lie" spent in 2006, while also becoming her second longest chart reign, spending eleven weeks at number one.[23] It has been certified 16× Platinum by the RIAA's Latin certifications program, denoting sales of over 960,000 units.[24] According to the 2017 year-end Nielsen Canada report, the song has sold 177,000 units in the country.[25] "Chantaje" went on to become the most successful Latin single of the decade by a female artist in the United States, according to Billboard.[2]

In the United Kingdom, the single became the first Spanish song by a female artist in history to be certified Silver for surpassing 200,000 equivalent units in the country.[26]
 
In France, the song debuted at number 36 on the week of 11 November 2016.[27] Later, it fell to numbers 91 and 126 in the following weeks, before climbing once again to number 76. After spending three weeks climbing on the charts, "Chantaje" cracked the top-forty for the second time, going to number forty.[27] Five weeks later, the song managed to climb from number 22 to number 14,[28] becoming Shakira's fifteenth top-twenty single and highest since "Dare (La La La)" (2014).

In Italy, "Chantaje" debuted at number 15 and peaked at number 11 for two weeks.[29]

In Netherlands, "Chantaje" managed to peak at number 18, becoming her highest-charting single since "Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)" (2010).[30]
 
In Switzerland, the song peaked at number 10, becoming Shakira's fifteenth top-ten single.[31]
 
In Spain, "Chantaje" entered the PROMUSICAE chart at number eight and reached number-one the following week, becoming Shakira's eighth number-one single.[32]

Music video[edit]
The music video was shot in Barcelona, on 13 and 14 October 2016, and it was directed by Spanish director and photographer Jaume de Laiguana, who has already directed various Shakira's music videos.[18] Cinematography was handled by Spanish cinematographer Xavi Giménez.[33] The official lyric video to the song was released on 16 November,[34] while the official music video was released on 18 November 2016.[35] In the beginning of the music video, as described by Rolling Stone's Sarah Grant, "Shakira strolls through a bodega with her pet pig on a leash and her wild mane of hair hidden under a pink wig."[16] "She then lures him in to an underground bar", as Billboard added,[35] while also "swivel[ing] her hips from the top of the bar to the men's bathroom, where she winds, kicks and grinds solo amid the urinals."[16]

Reception[edit]
The music video earned 100 million views in just 19 days, breaking the previous 21 days record, and becoming the fastest Spanish video ever to do so.[36] On 7 April 2017, it reached 1 billion views, becoming the fastest Spanish video to hit the billion visits landmark.[37] It was also the second-most viewed video on Vevo in 2017, after "Despacito".[38]

Salsa version[edit]
On 2 February, Shakira celebrated her birthday with a salsa version of "Chantaje" with Chelito de Castro.[39][40]

Live performances[edit]
Maluma performed the song in Valparaíso at the Viña del Mar International Song Festival in February 2017, then on his various tours since, where he typically has a female vocalist stand-in for Shakira's vocals. 

Shakira performed "Chantaje" with Coldplay's lead vocalist Chris Martin at the Global Citizen Festival in Hamburg in July 2017. She tried to get him to sing and understand the Spanish words. Shakira subsequently performed the song, solo, during her El Dorado World Tour in 2018.

Shakira performed a shortened, Salsa-inspired version of the song with Bad Bunny during her medley of songs at the Super Bowl LIV halftime show in 2020.[41][42]

On 12 April 2025, Shakira and Maluma performed the song together for the very first time during Shakira’s Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour in Medellin.[43]

"Ay Vamos"  [sic] (English: "Here We Go") is a song performed by Colombian singer J Balvin, released as the lead single of the reissue of his second studio album, La Familia B Sides, by Universal Music Mexico on 22 July 2014.

It received a nomination for the Billboard Latin Music Award for Latin Rhythm Airplay Song of the Year in 2015.[1] A remix, featuring French Montana and Nicky Jam was released on the Furious 7 soundtrack.

As of December 2024, the music video has received over 2 billion views on YouTube.[2]

"Ay Vamos"  [sic] (English: "Here We Go") is a song performed by Colombian singer J Balvin, released as the lead single of the reissue of his second studio album, La Familia B Sides, by Universal Music Mexico on 22 July 2014.

It received a nomination for the Billboard Latin Music Award for Latin Rhythm Airplay Song of the Year in 2015.[1] A remix, featuring French Montana and Nicky Jam was released on the Furious 7 soundtrack.

As of December 2024, the music video has received over 2 billion views on YouTube.[2]

"'''Taki Taki'''" is a song by French-Algerian DJ and record producer [[DJ Snake]], featuring American singer [[Selena Gomez]], Puerto Rican singer [[Ozuna]], and Dominican-American rapper [[Cardi B]]. The song was released on 28 September 2018 as the second single from DJ Snake's second studio album ''[[Carte Blanche (DJ Snake album)|Carte Blanche]]'' (2019).<ref name="release">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8477330/dj-snake-taki-taki-featuring-selena-gomez-ozuna-cardi-b |title=DJ Snake Charms With 'Taki Taki' Featuring Selena Gomez, Ozuna and Cardi B: Stream It Now |date=28 September 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=28 September 2018}}</ref> It was written and arranged by Bava (aka Ava Brignol), Belcalis Almanzar, Jorden Thorpe, Juan Carlos Ozuna Rosado, Juan G. Rivera, Max Borghetti, Selena Gomez, Vicente Saavedra, William Grigahcine. Ozuna opens the [[moombahton]] and [[reggaeton|reggaetón]] song in Spanish, while Cardi B and Gomez follow in both English and Spanish.

The song's music video, directed by [[Colin Tilley]], was released on 9 October 2018 and features the four artists and several dancers inside of an ancient temple ruin within a volcano. The single reached number one in sixteen countries (including Argentina, Portugal and Spain), several of which were outside the [[Hispanophone]] market. It received a Diamond [[Music recording certification|certification]] in France, went [[RIAA certification|quadruple Platinum]] in the US, and won nine [[music award]]s. "Taki Taki" made Cardi B the first female rapper to top the [[Spotify]] [[List of most-streamed songs on Spotify#Weekly number-one songs|Global]] chart,<ref name="spotify"/> extended her record as the first female rapper with [[List of most-streamed songs on Spotify|multiple billion-streamers]] on the platform,<ref name="first"/> and made Ozuna the artist with the most one billion-view videos on [[YouTube]].<ref name="billion"/>

==Background==
In July 2018, Cardi B confirmed a collaboration with DJ Snake, Ozuna and [[Selena Gomez|a third mystery guest]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8464772/cardi-b-confirms-dj-snake-collaboration-video |title=Cardi B Confirms DJ Snake Collaboration For Producer's New Album: Watch |last=Bein |first=Kat |date=10 July 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=28 September 2018}}</ref> The following month, [[Selena Gomez]] and Cardi B teased a behind-the-scenes look at the song's music video shoot, which was filmed in [[Los Angeles]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/8472167/selena-gomez-teases-dj-snakes-taki-taki-video-shoot-with-cardi-b-ozuna-see-the |title=Selena Gomez Teases DJ Snake's 'Taki Taki' Video Shoot With Cardi B & Ozuna: See the Photos |last=Peters |first=Mitchell |date=25 August 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=28 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8472151/cardi-b-collab-dj-snake-selena-gomez-ozuna |title=Cardi B Teases Collab With DJ Snake, Selena Gomez & Ozuna |last=Aniftos |first=Rania |date=24 August 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=28 September 2018}}</ref> On 17 September 2018, DJ Snake announced the release date.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/latin/8475406/dj-snake-announces-release-date-taki-taki-tweet |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180917200837/https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/latin/8475406/dj-snake-announces-release-date-taki-taki-tweet |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 September 2018 |title=DJ Snake Announces Release Date For 'Taki Taki' With Selena Gomez, Cardi B & Ozuna |last=Fernandez |first=Suzette |date=17 September 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=4 October 2018}}</ref>

==Composition==
"Taki Taki", a reference to percussion and drum beats, is classed primarily as a moombahton and reggaetón song.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.elmundo.es/f5/escucha/2018/09/28/5bae1800268e3ee1658b4650.html|title=Taki Taki, de DJ Snake, Selena Gómez, Ozuna y Cardi B: letra en español |date=28 September 2018 |work=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]] |language=es |access-date=3 October 2018}}</ref><ref name="rolling stone"/><ref>{{cite web|title= DJ Snake's "Taki Taki" with Selena Gomez, Ozuna, & Cardi B gets Official Music Video|url=https://www.youredm.com/2018/10/13/dj-snakes-taki-taki-with-selena-gomez-ozuna-cardi-b-gets-official-music-video/|date=13 October 2018|first=Matthew|last=Meadow|publisher=YourEDM|access-date=30 December 2018}}</ref> The whistle sample (in the [[Hook (music)|hook]]) is from ''Sounds of [[KSHMR]] Vol.2''. The track runs for three minutes and thirty-two seconds. Ozuna opens the track and provides the chorus, while Cardi B and Gomez follow, performing in English and Spanish.<ref name="rolling stone">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-latin/dj-snake-taki-taki-cardi-b-ozuna-selena-gomez-730414/ |title=Hear DJ Snake, Cardi B, Ozuna, Selena Gomez on All-Star Reggaeton Song 'Taki Taki' |last=Exposito |first=Susy |date=28 September 2018 |magazine=Rolling Stone |access-date=28 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.xxlmag.com/rap-music/new-music/2018/09/dj-snake-taki-taki-cardi-b-ozuna-selena-gomez/ |title=DJ Snake "Taki Taki" Featuring Cardi B, Ozuna and Selena Gomez: Listen To The New Song |last=Burks |first=Tosten |date=28 September 2018 |work=XXL |access-date=28 September 2018}}</ref>

Lyrically, the song sees Ozuna expressing his style of seduction, inviting his love interest to dance and interpreting what the other is thinking.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/latin/dj-snake-taki-taki-lyric-translation-8477355/ |title=Ozuna Tries to Seduce Cardi B and Selena Gomez in 'Taki Taki' Lyric Translation |last=Fernandez |first=Suzette |date=28 September 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=10 October 2018}}</ref>

Sheet music for "Taki Taki" showed the key of [[C-sharp minor|C♯ minor]] in [[time signature|common time]] with a fast tempo of 96 beats per minute.<ref>[https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0191613 Taki Taki]</ref>

==Music videos==
[[File:DJ Snake - Taki Taki (music video screenshot).png|thumb|From left to right, DJ Snake, Selena Gomez, Cardi B and Ozuna performing on an active [[lava field]].]]
The music video for "Taki Taki" premiered on 9 October 2018 on DJ Snake's YouTube channel. The video was directed by [[Colin Tilley]]. A short teaser clip was shown at the [[American Music Awards of 2018|2018 American Music Awards]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8478449/dj-snake-taki-taki-trailer-video |title=Watch the Trailer For DJ Snake, Selena Gomez, Cardi B & Ozuna's 'Taki Taki' Video |last=Bein |first=Kat |date=5 October 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=5 October 2018}}</ref> The video is set in a [[post-apocalyptic]] world.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8479155/dj-snake-taki-taki-video-featuring-selena-gomez-ozuna-cardi-b |title=DJ Snake Unveils Apocalyptic 'Taki Taki' Video Featuring Selena Gomez, Ozuna & Cardi B: Watch |last=Aniftos |first=Rania |date=9 October 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=9 October 2018}}</ref> The clip transitions with various landscapes showing the quartet together with a volcano in the background and in the solo scenes. These scenes include DJ Snake out in the storm near a [[Range Rover]], Ozuna in a women-filled pit, Cardi B wearing a black bodysuit covered by a black cape accompanied by dancers, and Gomez in a green monochromatic outfit in the forest.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.glamour.com/story/cardi-b-selena-gomez-taki-taki-music-video |title=Cardi B and Selena Gomez's "Taki Taki" Music Video Is the Only Thing You Need to See Tonight |last=Park |first=Andrea |date=9 October 2018 |work=Glamour |access-date=10 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/dj-snake-cardi-b-ozuna-selena-gomez-taki-taki-video-735459/ |title=Watch DJ Snake, Cardi B, Ozuna, Selena Gomez in Fantastical 'Taki Taki' Video |last=Reed |first=Ryan |date=9 October 2018 |magazine=Rolling Stone |access-date=10 October 2018}}</ref> It became the fifth fastest video of 2018 to reach 100 million views, and ranked among the top 10 fastest overall.<ref name="youtube">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/8480882/dj-snake-taki-taki-100-million-views-youtube |title=DJ Snake's 'Taki Taki' Surpasses 1 billion YouTube Views in just 3 months |last=Aniftos |first=Rania |date=19 October 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=19 October 2018}}</ref> "Taki Taki" made Ozuna the artist with the most 1 billion-view videos on YouTube, with over seven videos.<ref name="billion">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/latin/ozuna-most-videos-billion-views-youtube-8496711/ |title=Ozuna Tops Justin Bieber to Become the Artist With the Most 1 Billion-View Videos on YouTube |last=Fernandez |first=Suzette |date=5 February 2019 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref> As of September 2025, the video has received over 2.7 billion views on [[YouTube]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ixkoVwKQaJg|title=DJ Snake - Taki Taki ft. Selena Gomez, Ozuna, Cardi B|work=YouTube|date=9 October 2018}}</ref>
 
A pixel video for "Taki Taki" was released on 11 December 2018 on YouTube, which featured animated pixel versions of the four artists dancing in various backgrounds.<ref name=pixel>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=anfOF0KP4JE|title=DJ Snake - Taki Taki Official Pixel Video ft. Selena Gomez, Ozuna, Cardi B|work=YouTube|date=11 December 2018}}</ref> The lyrics "Booty explota como ''nagasaki''" (Booty blows up like Nagasaki) was criticized by Japanese media for belittling the [[atomic bombing of Nagasaki]] and the experience of its survivors.<ref>{{Cite web|title=「尻が長崎のように爆発」 世界的ヒット曲の歌詞が波紋：朝日新聞デジタル|url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASLC94QDVLC9PTIL00P.html|access-date=2021-07-13|website=朝日新聞デジタル|date=12 November 2018 |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Acts of insensitivity toward A-bomb devastation of Hiroshima and Nagasaki|url=http://www.hiroshimapeacemedia.jp/?p=88481|access-date=2021-07-13|website=Hiroshima Peace Media Center|language=en}}</ref> The lyrics were changed to "Booty explota como saki saki" (Booty blows up like saki saki), as requested by [[Universal Music LLC]].{{ref|pixel}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201811140054.html|title=Nagasaki lyrics pulled from global hit dance song 'Taki Taki'|work=The Asahi Shimbun|date=14 November 2018}}</ref>  This change in the lyrics was made in the official video.
In France, the music video were criticized following suggestive scenes, Cardi B's sexual poses and was broadcast with blurring and a warning "Not advised to kids under 10 years old" or without warning.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

==Commercial performance==
In the United States, "Taki Taki" debuted at number one on the [[Hot Latin Songs]], where Ozuna replaced himself at the top with "[[Te Boté]]", while bowing at number 27 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/dj-snake-selena-gomez-ozuna-cardi-b-taki-taki-hot-latin-songs/ |title=DJ Snake, Selena Gomez, Ozuna & Cardi B's 'Taki Taki' Debuts at No. 1 on Hot Latin Songs Chart |last=Bustios |first=Pamela |date=8 October 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=9 October 2018}}</ref> It eventually reached number 11 on the Hot 100 during its fourth week.<ref name="Hot 100 peak">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/maroon-5-cardi-b-rule-hot-100-sixth-week/|title=Maroon 5 and Cardi B Rule Billboard Hot 100 For Sixth Week, Post Malone and Swae Lee Debut in Top 10|magazine=Billboard|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=29 October 2018|access-date=30 October 2018}}</ref> It became Gomez's 16th consecutive top 40 entry on the Hot 100, the longest active run of any artist.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/selena-gomez-maroon-5-hot-100-chart-moves/ |title=Hot 100 Chart Moves: Selena Gomez's 'Back to You' Hits Top 40, Maroon 5's 'Girls Like You' Debuts |date=5 June 2018|magazine=Billboard |access-date=12 October 2018}}</ref> In the US [[Latin Airplay]] chart, it became the first number one for both DJ Snake and Gomez, the eighth for Ozuna and third for Cardi B.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/dj-snake-taki-taki-no-1-latin-airplay-chart/ |title=DJ Snake's Star-Powered 'Taki Taki' Hits No. 1 on Latin Airplay Chart |last=Bustios |first=Pamela |date=8 December 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=8 December 2018}}</ref>

In addition, "Taki Taki" reached number one in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Greece, Guatemala, Honduras, Israel, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Portugal, Spain and Venezuela; the song also reached the top 10 in Belgium, Canada, Chile, Costa Rica, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Paraguay, the Philippines, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Sweden and Switzerland; as well as the top 20 in Austria, Finland, Ireland, Lebanon, New Zealand, Norway, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The song had a strong international impact, reaching the top of the [[Spotify]] Global 50 chart where it has stayed for over four weeks. This made Cardi B the first female rapper to achieve such a feat.<ref name="spotify">{{Cite news |url=https://hiphopdx.com/editorials/id.4163/title.instagram-flexin-cardi-b-becomes-1st-female-rapper-to-top-spotifys-global-chart|title=Instagram Flexin: Cardi B Becomes 1st Female Rapper To Top Spotify's Global Chart|date=7 October 2018 |work=Hip Hop DX |access-date=9 October 2018}}</ref> It became DJ Snake's third song to reach [[List of most-streamed songs on Spotify|a billion streams]] on Spotify, as well as Cardi's third and Gomez's and Ozuna's first.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/9398039/dj-snake-taki-taki-billion-plays-spotify|title=This DJ Snake Track Reached a Billion Plays on Spotify|magazine=Billboard}}</ref> Cardi B extended her record as the first female rapper with multiple billion-streamers, until being surpassed by black females rappers [[Nicki Minaj]] (7 songs) and [[Doja Cat]] (8 songs).<ref name="first">{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/number-day-dj-snakes-taki-taki-amasses-billion-123020865.html|title=Number of the day: DJ Snake's 'Taki Taki' amasses a billion plays on Spotify|work=Yahoo!|author=[[Agence France-Presse]]|date=June 9, 2020}}</ref> As of November 2018, the song has reached number one on the official charts of 15 countries and the top 10 of 33 countries around the world.

In France, the song debuted at number thirteen on September 26, 2018, becoming for three of four artists the highest-debut since Gomez's own solo song "[[Good For You (Selena Gomez song)|Good For You]]", served as the lead single from her second album [[Revival (Selena Gomez album)|Revival]], which debuted at number 14.
Several weeks later and after [[Christmas music|Christmas time]], the song peaked at number 2 on January 5, 2019, blocked by "Tout Oublier" by [[Belgium|Belgian]] artist [[Angèle]] becoming DJ Snake's sixth top ten, Gomez's third, Cardi B's second and last top ten and Ozuna's first top ten.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lescharts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=DJ+Snake+feat%2E+Selena+Gomez%2C+Ozuna+%26+Cardi+B&titel=Taki+Taki&cat=s|title=Les charts - DJ Snake, Selena Gomez, Ozuna & Cardi B - Taki Taki|work=les charts.com|date=January 5, 2019|access-date=September 24, 2025}}</ref>

Although it failed to peak atop, the single is currently certified diamond in France and spent 57 weeks, becoming Ozuna, Gomez's and Cardi B longest-running song and DJ Snake second longest running song after "[[Loco Contigo]]".

==Live performances==
Ozuna and Cardi B performed the song together live for the first time at the Dominican Republic's ''Electric Paradise Festival'' on 22 December 2018.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/8491335/cardi-b-major-lazer-j-balvin-ozuna-dominican-republic-electric-paradise-festival |title=Cardi B, Major Lazer, J Balvin & More Highlight Dominican Republic's Electric Paradise Festival 2018 |last=Smith-Strickland|first=Stephanie |date=23 December 2018 |magazine=Billboard |access-date=23 December 2018}}</ref> Ozuna also performed the song at the [[Premio Lo Nuestro 2019|2019 Premios Lo Nuestro]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.univision.com/shows/premio-lo-nuestro/reggaeton-hecho-historia-premio-lo-nuestro-reunio-a-los-mas-grandes-en-un-show-con-mucha-gasolina |title=Reggaeton hecho historia: Premio Lo Nuestro reunió a los más grandes en un show con mucha 'gasolina' |date=21 February 2019 |work=Univision |access-date=22 February 2019 |language=es}}</ref> On 15 March 2019, he performed the song as part of a medley with "[[Baila Baila Baila]]" on ''[[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon]]''. The only time in which all four artists—DJ Snake, Ozuna, Cardi B and Selena Gomez—took to the stage together was during DJ Snake's set at the 2019 [[Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival]] in [[Indio, California]], much to the audience’s excitement. Ozuna featured the song during his headlining set and livestreamed performance at the [[Viña del Mar International Song Festival|Viña Del Mar International Song Festival]], in [[Valparaíso]], [[Chile]], on 28 February 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Taki Taki |first=Ozuna |date=28 February 2020 |title=Taki Taki - Viña Del Mar |website=[[YouTube]] |url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=WtAYcvKq0_k&pp=ygUOdGFraSB0YWtpIGxpdmU%3D }}</ref> He also performed the song during the ''[[Celebrating America]]'' inauguration special in 2021.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/latin/luis-fonsi-ozuna-celebrating-america-performance-9514206/|title=Ozuna & Luis Fonsi Perform 'Taki Taki' & 'Despacito' at 'Celebrating America' Special|last=Flores|first=Griselda |date=20 January 2021|magazine=Billboard |access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref>
